name: My Son Museum
kicker: Gallery beside the stream, before the towers
summary: Cham stone gallery at the gate: see the sculpture in a short stop before the cart to the towers. The building sits beside the Khe Thẻ stream, about 2 km from the brick, and cars end here. Give it the start of the morning. The towers are the day.
dotReason: A short stop on the way in, not a trip of its own
timeNeeded: A short stop before the cart
getThere: Cars stop here. 45 km by road from Hoi An
heroCaption: A carved pedestal in the gallery, with the hall behind it

notice.title: Check the gallery door if you arrive late
notice.body: The gallery is published as 06:00–17:00. Valley visiting runs to 18:00. If you arrive late, look at the door before you count on the room.

body: Stop at this building before you take the cart. It stands beside the Khe Thẻ stream, about 2 km northwest of the towers. Work ran from June 2004 to March 2005 with a Japanese government grant, and it has been the gateway since 2005. The room is there so you can see the site in outline before you go in. Cars end here. The electric cart leaves from here toward the towers.

The labels follow the group the piece came from. In the room: a linga-yoni from B1, 8th century; an undated stone pillar; a guardian from group E, 10th to 11th century; a Shiva from A4, 10th century; a corner flame ornament from H1, 13th century; a praying-figure relief of about the 12th to the 13th century; a dancing Shiva from H1, 13th century; a dancing Shiva relief from C1, 18th century; an elephant-lion from C1, 11th century; an altar piece from group A, 9th century; an Indra from group A, 10th century; and a Brahma from tower K, 11th century. The gallery holds 93 objects, and 708 more are displayed among the towers. A wooden sanctuary roof stands over a linga in the same room. That model has no published date.

Give it the start of the morning. The towers are the valley. Leave food outside the monument area, and leave the brick unclimbed once you leave this room. The entrance ticket covers the museum, the cart, a Cham folk performance, and the monuments. If the window sells the gallery apart from the towers, ask before you pay.

figures.caption: A wooden sanctuary roof over a linga, in the same gallery
figures.alt: A wooden model of a Cham sanctuary roof over a stone linga in the My Son gallery

gettingThere: Cars stop at this building. An electric cart covers about 2 km along the Khe Thẻ stream from here to the towers, and that ride is inside the entrance ticket. There is no train into the valley. Tourism bus 01DL, from Hoi An, is paused for six months from 15 Sep 2026.

legs.heading: From Hoi An
legs.body: By road, 45 km. Hire a car. Bus 01DL is paused from 15 Sep 2026 for six months.

legs.heading: From the towers
legs.body: The electric cart runs about 2 km back to the museum along the Khe Thẻ stream. The carts run from the museum toward the Nhà Đôi area.

hours: 06:00–17:00 for the gallery. Valley visiting runs to 18:00.
admissionNote: No separate adult price. A non-resident adult is listed at 150,000 VND and a Vietnamese adult at 100,000 VND, including VAT. The purchase page showed 148,000 VND and 99,000 VND on 21 Oct 2026. Read the amount before you pay. The ticket covers the museum, the cart, a Cham folk performance, and the monuments. Children from 5 to 15 buy the 30,000 VND shuttle ticket. Children under 5 are free.
